message.content:
You are writing and recording live Obsidian CDP scenarios for PR DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1627 (ENG-2490), which clears Obsidian scanner ESLint errors in apps/obsidian. The goal: a real screen-recorded mp4 per test case below, showing the behaviour works, plus a pass/fail matrix. Do not edit any repo source file; all scenario code lives in the scratchpad.

## Paths
- Worktree (run commands from here): /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-2490-fix-the-obsidian-scanners-blocking-eslint-errors
- Plugin source: <worktree>/apps/obsidian/src
- Scratchpad CDP dir (put new files here): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-trang-doan-Desktop-code-discourse-graph/dad56eb0-85c8-43af-afe3-79e3dc24c31b/scratchpad/cdp
- Videos land in: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-trang-doan-Desktop-code-discourse-graph/dad56eb0-85c8-43af-afe3-79e3dc24c31b/scratchpad/videos

## Read first (conventions and helpers to reuse)
- Skill docs: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/SKILL.md (scenario contract, ctx, gotchas). Driver: same dir scripts/driver.mjs.
- Helpers: cdp/lib.mjs (cmd, openNote, mouse, move, click, dblclick, key, sleep), cdp/canvaslib.mjs (openCanvas, dropNode, shapes, centerOf, grabEditor, NT node-type ids, fm frontmatter, consoleTrap/Release, readState/writeState).
- Worked examples: cdp/s-modal.mjs (modal popover geometry helpers), cdp/s-canvas.mjs (canvas fixture C0 creates canvas + Evidence/Claim nodes + a 'supports' relation and stores ids in canvas-state.json; many canvas interactions), cdp/s-sidebar.mjs (discourse context sidebar + wikilink badge popover chips).
- Recorder: cdp/rec.mjs exports `recorded(scenarios, { prefix })`, which wraps each scenario so its run() is screencast-recorded (with a cursor dot, caption = scenario name, paced mouse input) into videos/<prefix>-NN-<firstword>.mp4. Use it; don't change its behaviour. Keep scenario names short and starting with an id like "N2.1".

## Running
`node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs --marker 'htmlLayer.hide()' --skip-build --scenario <file.mjs>` from the worktree. The vault "Obsidian Vault" is already leased to this worktree and has the branch build loaded. IMPORTANT: another CDP recording run may hold the vault's lock right now. If run.mjs exits 2 / reports a lock, do not take or touch the vault; keep writing scenarios and retry later (`node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/doctor.mjs` shows the lock). Never quit Obsidian, never pick another vault, never use bare `git stash`. Calibrate scenarios with plain (unrecorded) runs first, then do a final recorded run via a wrapper module like `export default recorded([...], { prefix: "b-..." })`. Notes you create belong under `_verify/<branch>/` via ctx.writeNote. Restore any setting you change in teardown.

## Test cases (each needs a scenario with a real assertion, then a recorded clip)
Use real input (CDP mouse/keys) for the user-facing step where feasible; programmatic setup is fine. Find exact labels/selectors in source (file:line hints from a prior trace below).
Node modal (ModifyNodeModal, components/ModifyNodeModal.tsx; assert: modal opens, title textarea present, and for popover routes the `.suggestion-container` appears under the title with position fixed, dTop 8, dLeft 0 after typing 2+ chars that match an existing node, e.g. "ev"/"cl"; for no-popover routes assert no popover):
 1. Editor right-click with text selected → "Turn into discourse node" → a type (index.ts:256-275). Popover.
 2. Node-tag hotkey (setting "Node tag hotkey", default `\`) with text selected → pick a type in InlineNodeTypePicker (index.ts:323-351, components/InlineNodeTypePicker.ts:143-158). Popover.
 3. Hover a node tag in the editor → tooltip button "Create {NodeType}" (utils/tagNodeHandler.ts:375-428). Popover.
 4. Hover an embedded image in the editor → "Convert to node" icon (utils/imageEmbedHoverIcon.ts:36-56). Popover, empty title. Needs a note embedding an image file in the vault.
 5. File explorer right-click on a non-node markdown note → "Convert into" → type (index.ts:216-251), and on an image file (index.ts:198-214). No popover. Two clips are fine, or one scenario doing both.
 6. Canvas right-click on a text shape → "Convert To" → type (components/canvas/CustomContextMenu.tsx:93-116), and on an image shape (convertToDiscourseNode.ts:167). Popover.
Sidebar:
 7. Wikilink relation-count badge popover in Reading view (utils/discourseContextOverlayPostProcessor.ts:98-106): open popover → "Add a new relation" → pick type → "You can link with" chips appear (see s-sidebar.mjs T3.5 for the Live Preview version).
Node shape (components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseNodeShape.tsx load effect):
 8. Node card "Context" tab → "Add this relation to canvas" (components/canvas/overlays/RelationPanel.tsx:234-273, 362-470): the new node shape gets a title = file basename and non-zero w/h (the load effect sizes it).
 9. Drag a wikilink (or its drag handle, utils/wikilinkDragHandler.ts:88-100) from a note onto the canvas, or the closest real-input equivalent: a discourse-node shape is created with correct title/size.
 10. Rename a note's file while its canvas is closed, reopen the canvas: shape title updates to the new basename.
Relation (components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationShape.tsx):
 11. Unlabelled relation: double-click/Enter to edit; indicator stays the path (no label rect) — compare g.tl-shape-indicator child tags as s-canvas.mjs indicatorSig does.
 12. Create a relation from the drag handles on a selected node (components/canvas/overlays/DragHandleOverlay.tsx:163-200, RelationTypeDropdown).
 13. Right-click a plain tldraw arrow bound between two nodes → "Relation" → type (CustomContextMenu.tsx:69-90, utils/convertArrowToDiscourseRelation.ts): becomes a discourse-relation bound both ends.
Binding (components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx):
 14. Group two bound nodes (Cmd+G): relation stays bound, no console errors, parent/index sane.
 15. Arrow-key nudge a selected bound node: relation follows, index stays above.
 16. Duplicate (Cmd+D) or copy+paste a relation alone (and with only one of its nodes): no uncaught errors; record what happens (count shapes/bindings).
 17. Same as 16 on a bent relation (set props.bend non-zero first).
Drawing (components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx getFontDefForExport):
 18. Export/copy a labelled relation as SVG (tldraw editor.getSvgString or the menu's "Copy as SVG/PNG"): the SVG contains an @font-face / font def for the label, and no errors.
For cases where behaviour must match main but you cannot run main, assert "no uncaught errors and sensible state", and say so in `expected`.

## Deliverable
Return: (a) the scenario file paths, (b) the final recorded run's pass/fail line per case with the actual values, (c) the list of mp4 paths with which case each shows, (d) anything you could not drive with real input or could not verify, stated plainly. If a case fails, check whether it is a scenario bug before reporting it as a product bug; never weaken an assertion just to pass.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.

# UI constraints

Always-on constraints for any UI edit in this monorepo. The Figma workflow, the token
values, and the per-app reference tables moved to the `figma-implementation` skill; invoke
it when implementing a design.

- **Check `packages/ui/src/components/ui/` before writing a new shared component.** Button,
  Card, Label, Checkbox, Select, Textarea and Badge already exist.
- **No hardcoded hex colors in shared components.** Use the Tailwind theme tokens from
  `packages/tailwind-config` or the CSS variables in `packages/ui/src/globals.css`.
- **The three apps do not share a UI stack.** `apps/website` uses `@repo/ui`; `apps/roam`
  uses BlueprintJS and deliberately does not use `@repo/ui`; `apps/obsidian` uses custom
  React with Tailwind mapped to Obsidian CSS variables.
- **Import across packages by `@repo/*` alias, never a relative path.**

TypeScript, naming, and general UI conventions live in `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.
